name: revert-mahi-backpressure-runtime

base_results.finding: current clean live reference before item253 runtime changes
observer relay queue bound produced retries and cut delivery
raising thresholds removed retries but still collapsed TPS and left Mahi pools backlogged

hypothesis: Items 253 and 254 show the new observer/owner backpressure runtime changes are the regression source. Reverting those runtime and Ansible env changes while keeping the decision-log artifacts should restore item-251-style green behavior.

rollback_verification.expectation: No diff for the touched runtime/env files versus the pre-item253 plan commit, excluding new experiment and decision-log artifacts.

live_steps.description: build release binary natively for Linux from the tagged rollback commit
deploy default three-ingress topology without item253 backpressure env lines
wipe state and restart default live topology
live_steps.command: cd chain/deploy/ansible && KOMBAT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(grep -m1 '^KOMBAT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=' /tmp/and-live-testnet/validator-1.env | cut -d= -f2-) .venv/bin/ansible kombat_live_testnet -m shell -a 'systemctl stop kombat-chain-ingress3 kombat-chain-ingress2 kombat-chain-ingress kombat-chain && rm -rf /var/lib/and-chain && mkdir -p /var/lib/and-chain/snapshots && chown -R and-chain:and-chain /var/lib/and-chain && systemctl start kombat-chain && systemctl start kombat-chain-ingress kombat-chain-ingress2 kombat-chain-ingress3'

result.reason: The runtime/env rollback removed the item253 backpressure surfaces but did not recover item251-class behavior. Throughput fell to 17,821.6 TPS, Mahi pools stayed heavily backlogged, and validator-4 diverged at common height 59. The loss of green behavior is not explained solely by the item253 runtime code.
